sp.p: Faith, sir, they are both as sure as love, a priest, and three thousand pound (which is her portion) can make ’em; and by this time are ready to bespeak their wedding supper at the Windmill, except some friend here prevent ’em and invite ’em home.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Marry, that will I; I thank thee for putting me in mind on’t. [To a Servant] Sirrah, go you and fetch ’em hither, upon my warrant. [Exit Servant.] Neither’s friends have cause to be sorry, if I know the young couple aright. [To Brainworm] Here, I drink to thee for thy good news. But, I pray thee, what hast thou done with my man Formal?

sp.speaker: BRAINWORM
sp.p: Faith, sir, after some ceremony passed, as making him drunk, first with story, and then with wine, but all in kindness, and stripping him to his shirt, I left him in that cool vein, departed, sold Your Worship’s warrant to these two, [Indicating Bobadill and Matthew] pawned his livery for that varlet’s gown to serve it in, and thus have brought myself, by my activity, to Your Worship’s consideration.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: And I will consider thee, in another cup of sack. Here’s to thee, which, having drunk off, this is my sentence. [He drinks.] Pledge me: Thou hast done or assisted to nothing, in my judgement, but deserves to be pardoned for the wit o’the offence. If thy master, or any man here, be angry with thee, I shall suspect his ingine while I know him for’t. [A noise is heard.] How now? What noise is that?

sp.speaker: SERVANT
sp.p: Sir, it is Roger is come home.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Bring him in, bring him in. FORMAL [is brought in] to them. What, drunk in arms, against me? Your reason, your reason for this?

sp.speaker: FORMAL
sp.p: I beseech Your Worship to pardon me. I happened into ill company by chance that cast me into a sleep and stripped me of all my clothes –

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Well, tell him I am Justice Clement, and do pardon him. But what is this to your armour? What may that signify?

sp.speaker: FORMAL
sp.p: An’t please you, sir, it hung up i’the room where I was stripped, and I borrowed it of one o’the drawers to come home in, because I was loath to do penance through the street i’my shirt.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Well, stand by awhile. [Enter] EDWARD KNOWELL, WELLBRED, [and] BRIDGET to them. Who be these? Oh, the young company. [To them] Welcome, welcome! Gi’ you joy. Nay, Mistress Bridget, blush not; you are not so fresh a bride but the news of it is come hither afore you. Master Bridegroom, I ha’ made your peace; give me your hand. So will I for all the rest, ere you forsake my roof.

sp.speaker: EDWARD KNOWELL
sp.p: We are the more bound to your humanity, sir.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Only these two [Indicating Bobadill and Matthew] have so little of man in ’em, they are no part of my care.

sp.speaker: WELLBRED
sp.p: Yes, sir, let me pray you for this gentleman; [Indicating Matthew] he belongs to my sister, the bride.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: In what place, sir?

sp.speaker: WELLBRED
sp.p: Of her delight, sir, below the stairs and in public: her poet, sir.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: A poet? I will challenge him myself presently, at extempore:

lg.l: Mount up thy Phlegon muse, and testify
How Saturn, sitting in an ebon cloud,
Disrobed his podex, white as ivory,
And through the welkin thundered all aloud.

sp.speaker: WELLBRED
sp.p: He is not for extempore, sir. He is all for the pocket muse; please you command a sight of it.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Yes, yes, search him for a taste of his vein.

sp.speaker: WELLBRED
sp.p: [To Matthew] You must not deny the Queen’s justice, sir, under a writ o’ rebellion.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: What, all this verse? Body o’me, he carries a whole ream, a commonwealth of paper, in’s hose! Let’s see some of his subjects.

lg.l: [He reads.] Unto the boundless ocean of thy face
Runs this poor river, charged with streams of eyes.
How? This is stol’n!

sp.speaker: EDWARD KNOWELL
sp.p: A parody! A parody! With a kind of miraculous gift to make it absurder than it was.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Is all the rest of this batch? Bring me a torch; lay it together, and give fire. Cleanse the air. Here was enough to have infected the whole city, if it had not been taken in time! [The poems are burnt.] See, see, how our poet’s glory shines! Brighter and brighter! Still it increases! Oh, now it’s at the highest; and now it declines as fast. You may see: Sic transit gloria mundi.

sp.speaker: KNOWELL
sp.p: There’s an emblem for you, son, and your studies!

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Nay, no speech or act of mine be drawn against such as profess it worthily. They are not born every year, as an alderman. There goes more to the making of a good poet than a sheriff, Master Kitely. You look upon me! Though I live i’the city here amongst you, I will do more reverence to him, when I meet him, than I will to the mayor, out of his year. But these paper-pedlars! These ink-dabblers! They cannot expect reprehension or reproach. They have it with the fact.

sp.speaker: EDWARD KNOWELL
sp.p: Sir, you have saved me the labour of a defence.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: It shall be discourse for supper between your father and me, if he dare undertake me. But to dispatch away these. [To Bobadill and Matthew] You sign o’the soldier, and picture o’the poet – but both so false I will not ha’ you hanged out at my door till midnight – while we are at supper, you two shall penitently fast it out in my court without; and, if you will, you may pray there that we may be so merry within as to forgive or forget you when we come out. [Indicating Formal] Here’s a third, because we tender your safety, shall watch you; he is provided for the purpose. [To Formal] Look to your charge, sir.

sp.speaker: STEPHEN
sp.p: And what shall I do?

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Oh, I had lost a sheep an he had not bleated! – Why, sir, you shall give Master Downright his cloak; and I will entreat him to take it. A trencher and a napkin you shall have i’the buttery, and keep Cob and his wife company here; whom I will entreat first to be reconciled, and you to endeavour with your wit to keep ’em so.

sp.speaker: STEPHEN
sp.p: I’ll do my best.

sp.speaker: COB
sp.p: Why, now I see thou art honest, Tib, I receive thee as my dear and mortal wife again.

sp.speaker: TIB
sp.p: And I you, as my loving and obedient husband.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: Good complement! It will be their bridal night, too. They are married anew. Come, I conjure the rest to put off all discontent. You, Master Down-right, your anger; you, Master Knowell, your cares; Master Kitely and his wife, their jealousy.

lg.l: For, I must tell you both, while that is fed,
Horns i’the mind are worse than o’the head.
Sir, thus they go from me. – Kiss me, sweetheart.
See, what a drove of horns fly in the air,
Winged with my cleansèd and my credulous breath!
Watch ’em, suspicious eyes, watch where they fall:
See, see, on heads that think they’ve none at all!
Oh, what a plenteous world of this will come!
When air rains horns, all may be sure of some. –
I ha’ learned so much verse out of a jealous man’s part in a play.

sp.speaker: CLEMENT
sp.p: ’Tis well, ’tis well! This night we’ll dedicate to friendship, love, and laughter. Master Bridegroom, take your bride and lead; every one, a fellow. Here is my mistress: Brainworm! To whom all my addresses of courtship shall have their reference. Whose adventures this day, when our grandchildren shall hear to be made a fable, I doubt not but it shall find both spectators and applause.
